newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy's Prodi welcomed in rebel-held Albanian town.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi welcomed in rebel-held Albanian town.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi received a thunderous welcome from thousands of Albanians in the rebel-held city of Vlore on Sunday.

Prodi, arriving by helicopter and escorted by heavily armed Italian marines, came to this city 150 km (90 miles) south of Tirana to express condolences to the victims of a boat disaster and pledge Italian support to help Albania out of its crisis.
Italy is leading a multinational mission to secure the supply of food and medicines to Albania, which Prodi said he hoped would help restore law and order.
"The mission is called 'Alba (dawn),'" Prodi said at a news conference. "And this could be the dawn in the history of Albania, the rebirth of Albania."
He said the 6,000-strong force was coming in peace. Its aim was to help a country that sank into near-anarchy after popular get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed.
"We do not intend to intervene in domestic Albanian politics," Prodi said before calling for a moment of silence for the victims of a refugee boat that sank on March 28 off the Italian coast.

Tirana said that 80 people were killed when the boat, which had left Vlore packed with refugees fleeing the violence, was rammed by the Italian ship, charges Italy denies. It was the worst maritime disaster in modern Albania's history.
Prodi planned to visit Vlore last week, but that was postponed because of a new outbreak of violence.
The town has been under rebel control since the start of the armed uprising in which nearly 300 people have been killed.
Prodi paid a brief visit to Gjirokaster, also in the south, on April 2. He was the first foreign leader to visit Europe's poorest country since its descent into lawlessness and violence.

About two dozen Italian marines were on the ground waiting for Prodi when he landed in an Italian army helicopter escorted by two other armed gunships near a lake about 10 km (six miles) outside Vlore.

Albania's Prime Minister Bashkim Fino was on hand to greet Prodi after arriving in his own helicopter. Prodi was also welcomed by the leader of the rebel group, the national salvation committee that controls the south.
"It is a privilege to have Prime Minister Prodi here in our city," said rebel leader Albert Shyti. "I do not think there will be any danger to the Italians here."
Thousands of cheering Albanians lined the road leading into Vlore as Prodi rode by in a motorcade of about 30 cars and armoured vehicles.
Banners reading "Welcome Mr Prodi" along with "We Want Our Money Back" were held up by spectators along the road into town.
An estimated 10,000 people jammed a central town square in front of a university building where Prodi and Fino met local leaders in the rebel stronghold.
Outside the meeting, the crowd also chanted profanities, in Italian, deriding President Sali Berisha, whom many southern Albanians blame for the chaos that sweeping the nation.
Prodi said Italy planned to open a consulate in Vlore. He said Italy and Albania would work together to encourage foreign investment in Albania.
